The region $D$ in the third quadrant is enclosed between two quarter-circles centered at $O$ of radii $3$ and $5,$ as shown above. What is 
${∬}_{D}3x\,\text{d}A$
expressed in polar coordinates?
worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form 

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

The region $D$ represents a portion of the washer enclosed between the circles of radii $3$ and $5$ centered at the origin. In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,3\le r\le 5,\,\pi \le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2}}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}3x\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}3(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{3}^{5}3{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
